EXPLANATION: The dominant Raman band at 2125 cm⁻¹ is characteristic of a C≡C stretching vibration from an internal alkyne; nitrile stretches would appear higher (≈2220–2260 cm⁻¹) and are therefore unlikely. No O-H band (≈3200-3600 cm⁻¹) is observed, arguing against the alcohol-containing candidates, and no N–H band suggests no amine. Candidate 2 (CC#CCC#CCCC) is the only purely hydrocarbon structure that contains internal alkynes (two C≡C bonds), matching the strong 2125 cm⁻¹ feature and explaining its relatively large width (overlap of two similar stretches). The remaining peaks (≈2900-3000 cm⁻¹ C–H stretches, 1430-1460 cm⁻¹ CH₂/CH₃ bends, and several skeletal modes 800-900 cm⁻¹) are consistent with an aliphatic hydrocarbon chain.
